screens.name: landing
strengths: The stained-glass mirror gives the experience a recognizable central object.
The headline has personality, and the primary button is unmistakable.
problems: The headline reflection crowds the introductory paragraph. Remove the reflected text or confine it to a shallower, lower-opacity strip.
The explanation introduces cards, guesses, archetypes and friends before play begins. Shorten the paragraph to one promise and move the friend-game teaser later.

screens.name: lobby
strengths: Three generously sized choices create an easy mobile decision.
The explanation that wording changes but answers count equally builds useful clarity.
problems: The purple outline on 'Make it fun' looks selected, but there is no visible confirmation action. For immediate navigation, add a trailing arrow to every choice and remove the default selected treatment.
Italic descriptions make all three options feel ceremonious and slow to scan. Use the body sans serif and reduce each description to one short sentence.

screens.name: chapter intro
strengths: The phone island communicates the chapter theme without needing an explanation.
The miniature mirror connects answering cards to a tangible collection mechanic.
problems: The illustration occupies almost the entire upper third while the chapter title arrives well below it. Reduce the illustration height by about 20% and move the title upward.
'0 of 40 shards' competes with '6 cards next' as the screen's progress message. Make '6 cards in this chapter' primary inside the panel and shrink total shard progress to a secondary line.

screens.name: scenario card
strengths: The specific family-photo scenario is more engaging than a conventional personality statement.
Large answer targets and clear separation make the choices easy to scan.
problems: The standing Genii instruction consumes two lines above an already explanatory card. Reduce it to one short line or show it only on the first card.
Each answer reserves a wide gutter for a decorative shard, narrowing the useful text area. Reduce the icon gutter to about 24 CSS pixels and give the answer text that space.

screens.name: reply card
strengths: Named speakers and chat bubbles turn the question into a believable social moment.
Reply-shaped choices distinguish this format from the standard scenario card.
problems: The setup repeats information already conveyed by the messages, pushing answers downward. Shorten it to 'Four months in. Your parent adds Sam to the family chat without asking.'
The selected reply relies on a thin purple border and pale tint. Add a checkmark and a stronger fill so selection survives glare and quick scanning.

screens.name: receipts card
strengths: The serrated paper, ruled rows and total form a coherent interaction metaphor.
'Tear it off' gives submission a distinctive, contextually appropriate verb.
problems: The oversized heading takes three lines before a long checklist. Reduce this format's heading size and shorten it to 'Money between friends. What have you done this year?'
'TOTAL 0' resembles a monetary amount in a money-themed receipt. Change the label to 'ITEMS CHECKED' so the number clearly counts selections.

screens.name: rank card
strengths: Numbered positions, FIRST/LAST labels and a separate confirmation button establish the ranking task clearly.
The fantasy premise introduces welcome variety late in the run.
problems: Each reorder handle combines dots and chevrons, leaving drag versus tap behavior ambiguous. Use a plain grip for dragging or distinct up/down buttons with separate targets.
The fourth row is taller than the others because of its copy. Shorten it to 'Weekday appointments. Weekends are mine.' so the ranking list has a more stable rhythm.

screens.name: late-run scenario
strengths: The fitted-sheet detail delivers a memorable comic escalation.
The evolved glass Genii and fuller mirror communicate progression within a consistent shell.
problems: The prompt breaks awkwardly after the opening quotation and takes five heavy lines. Set the quote inline with the setup and reduce the prompt size slightly.
The large home island is mostly decorative below the task while Genii remains small and peripheral. Reduce the island's glow and size, then give Genii a little more space beside its line.

screens.name: lock
strengths: The shift to deep violet creates a convincing dramatic threshold.
Eight orbiting cards make the prediction mechanic immediately tangible.
problems: 'Your last 8 cards' can mean cards already answered. Change it to 'Genii predicts your next 8 answers. The guesses lock before you play.'
The numbered explanation, lock panel and disclaimer repeat related information. Condense them into two short steps and one compact lock notice to bring the button upward.

screens.name: two archetypes
strengths: The divided mirror gives the two-archetype idea a strong visual structure.
Large serif names create a reveal worth pausing on.
problems: The six adjective chips compete with the archetypes and the closing line. Move the chips to the traits screen and let the two names dominate.
The bottom-right Next control looks disabled because of its muted text and border. Give it an opaque surface and high-contrast text, with the same visible control on every reveal screen.

screens.name: character sheet
strengths: The people/life grouping carries the two-sided identity concept into the detailed results.
Signature and wild-card treatments create useful distinctions within the six stats.
problems: Six dense cards leave no visible breathing room or navigation at the bottom. Shorten each description to one line and reduce card padding enough to reserve a navigation footer.

Diamond counts, 'Clear' and 'Off the charts' mix apparent magnitude with confidence, while the wild card is also labeled Clear. Use one explicitly named scale and replace the wild-card strength label with 'Mixed signal'.

screens.name: what Genii knows best
strengths: The enlarged leading result establishes a clear first read.
Faceted badges connect the result language to the mirror's material vocabulary.
problems: This screen repeats all six stats immediately after the character sheet. Keep only the strongest result and two supporting signals; remove the remaining three rows.
The lavender trait names lose emphasis against the translucent purple panels. Use near-white for the names and reserve lavender for the smaller category labels.

screens.name: room by room
strengths: The chapter islands return as useful contextual illustrations rather than unrelated decoration.
Everyday situations make the abstract result labels easier to understand.
problems: The result pills occupy the same line as the room headings and make the longest heading feel cramped. Move each pill beneath its heading or replace it with a small text label.

'They've stopped arguing about it' asserts other people's behavior without showing support. Replace it with a player-centered statement such as 'You want closeness without handing over the decisions.'

screens.name: Genii's calls
strengths: The large 5 of 8 provides a clear payoff for the prediction mechanic.
Showing misses alongside correct calls makes the outcome feel more credible.
problems: Bright gradients wash out white titles and status text on the successful tiles. Give all tiles a darker, more opaque fill and keep the bright glow at the border.
Some correct tiles say CALLED IT while others show only a trait pill. Give all eight tiles the same title/status/detail structure, with an explicit outcome label in every tile.

screens.name: share card
strengths: The preview makes the output concrete before asking the player to share.
Story/Post and Night/Day are concise, understandable customization controls.
problems: The exported card combines rays, world scenery, mirror facets, Genii and tiny trait pills. Hide the rays and trait pills in this template so the archetype names remain legible at feed size.

Share image, Challenge a friend, Copy link and the opposite-type prompt create too many competing exits. Keep Share image primary, Challenge a friend secondary, and move Copy link and the opposite prompt behind the friend action.

screens.name: get the app
strengths: The real game-world scene gives the destination more substance than a generic download advertisement.
The dark install button is clearly separated from the luminous background.
problems: The hero labels 'Miia lives it' but visually centers Genii, leaving the promised digital twin unidentified. Reposition the label beside a clearly identifiable Miia depiction and label Genii separately if both remain.

The headline and paragraph repeat a broad promise without making the first action concrete. Replace the paragraph with a short line beginning 'Start with a lunch photo' and trim the lower links into one compact secondary row.

top_fixes: Create a shared reveal footer with visible Back and Next controls; reserve its space on every slide and keep controls clear of content and the phone's safe area.
Replace the calls screen's luminous tile interiors with a consistent dark violet fill; retain glow only around the edges and use the same explicit outcome label placement on every tile.
Remove the bottom three rows from 'What Genii knows best' and present only the signature result plus two supporting signals, eliminating the most obvious repetition in the reveal.
Standardize result terminology: explicitly label what the diamonds measure, use one set of strength words, and replace 'Clear' on the wild card with 'Mixed signal'.
Remove reflected headline text on landing and chapter screens; reduce large question headings slightly where they wrap beyond four lines.
Reduce the shared answer-icon gutter and shorten the standing Genii instruction to one line, reclaiming space across all standard question cards.
Simplify the share template by hiding the radial rays and tiny adjective pills; preserve the two archetype names, mirror, Genii and a readable brand address.
Rewrite the lock explanation to say 'next 8 answers' and reposition the app-handoff label so the image clearly identifies Miia.
hooks: The set holds attention through specific comic writing, varied card formats and a coherent mirror mechanic. The strongest screenshot moment is the lock: deep violet, the completed mirror and eight orbiting cards finally create dramatic contrast. Make it stronger by shortening the explanation and stating precisely that the guesses lock before the next eight answers. The reveal loses momentum through repeated six-stat summaries and long stretches of similarly weighted panels. Static captures do not establish animation quality, touch responsiveness or whether the Stories pacing supports reading.
brand_fit: The violet palette, glass materials, islands and assembled mirror form a recognizable world, and the orb-to-glass-slime evolution fits Genii well. The main gap is hierarchy: nearly everything receives glow, translucency, a rounded container or a decorative backdrop, so extraordinary moments have too little room to feel extraordinary. Genii also remains peripheral during much of play, while the app handoff visually blurs Genii and Miia. More opaque reading surfaces, fewer simultaneous effects and clearer character roles would make this feel more deliberately authored.

meta.judge: Codex CLI, read-only, ephemeral, same 16-screen list and prompt shape as R3 and R4
meta.prompt_note: neutral: no prior scores and no list of changes; the map screen is named the character sheet
